question: In 1995 a New York court treated Prodigy as publisher of a user's defamatory post; CompuServe had escaped in 1991. Why the difference?
answer: Prodigy screened its boards. In Cubby v. CompuServe, a service that did not review posts was treated like a bookshop, unaware of what it stocked; in Stratton Oakmont v. Prodigy, a service that policed content was treated as a publisher. Moderating raised the risk. Congress removed that penalty in 1996, in Section 230.
move: Check whether a rule punishes the people who try hardest to comply.
ask: Which rule in my world punishes the people trying hardest to do right?
trap: Assuming the careful host must be the safer one in law.
source: Stratton Oakmont v. Prodigy, N.Y. Sup. Ct., 1995
reference: Stratton Oakmont, Inc. v. Prodigy Services Co., 1995 WL 323710 (N.Y. Sup. Ct. 24 May 1995)
